q.t: The SI unit of length is the…
q.e: The metre, symbol m.

q.t: 1 km = how many m?
q.e: Kilo means thousand.

q.t: 1 m = how many cm?
q.e: Centi means hundredth.

q.t: 1 cm = how many mm?
q.e: 10 millimetres make a centimetre.

q.t: Every measurement has two parts: a number and a…
q.e: '13 handspans' = number 13, unit handspan.

q.t: A swing moves in…
q.e: It moves to and fro about a fixed position.

q.t: A merry-go-round moves in…
q.e: Along a circular path.

q.t: A falling orange moves in…
q.e: Along a straight line.

q.t: To measure the girth of a tree, use a…
q.e: A rigid scale can't wrap around.

q.t: Which is written correctly?
q.e: Lowercase, no s, no full stop, space before the unit.

q.t: Why do five friends get different results measuring a table in handspans?
q.e: Body-part units differ from person to person.

q.t: The smallest division on a 15 cm scale is…
q.e: So 1 mm is the smallest length you can measure with it.

q.t: Where should your eye be when reading a scale?
q.e: Looking at an angle gives a wrong reading.

q.t: A scale's zero is broken. One end of a pencil is at 1.0 cm, the other at 10.4 cm. Length (cm)?
A point from which distance is measured is called a…
q.e: Everyone agrees only when measuring from the same reference point.

q.t: An object is in motion if its position changes with time relative to…
q.e: Motion is always relative to something.

q.t: Motion that repeats after a fixed time interval is…
q.e: Both circular and oscillatory motion are periodic.

q.t: How do you measure a curved line?
o: Lay a thread along it, straighten and measure
q.e: The thread follows the curve; then measure it straight.

q.t: 1 inch = ?
q.e: The inch is an older unit still used by some.

q.t: An ancient Indian unit of length based on finger width is…
q.e: Still used by traditional carpenters and tailors.

q.t: How many mm in 3.5 cm?
How many cm in 2.3 m?
How many m in 4.5 km?
Deepa sits in a moving bus. Relative to the bus, other passengers are…
q.e: Their positions don't change relative to the bus.

q.t: Relative to a building outside, the same passengers are…
q.e: Both answers are correct — it depends on the reference point.

q.t: Kilometre stones read 'Delhi 70 km' then 'Delhi 60 km'. The reference point is…
q.e: Distances are stated relative to Delhi.

q.t: Which pair are both periodic?
q.e: Both repeat their path after fixed intervals.

q.t: Which would you measure in kilometres?
q.e: Use km for large lengths.

q.t: Why did countries adopt SI units?
o: So measurements of the same length don't differ
q.e: Standard units give everyone the same result.

q.t: A pressed metal strip springing up and down shows…
q.e: It moves to and fro about a fixed position.

q.t: A pencil's ends read 2.0 cm and 13.7 cm on a scale. Length (cm)?
How many mm in 1 m?
1 mm = ? cm
q.e: 10 mm = 1 cm, so 1 mm = 0.1 cm.

q.t: Two friends disagree on whether the garden or school is closer. Both are right because…
o: They measure from different reference points (their homes)
q.e: Use the same reference point to agree.

q.t: Which is NOT a correct way to write a length?
q.e: Never add 's' for plural.

q.t: An eraser whirled on a thread moves in…
q.e: It goes round a circular path.

q.t: A march-past is an example of…
q.e: Soldiers march in straight lines.

q.t: Ruled markings found at Harappan sites suggest…
q.e: Possible scales excavated from Harappan sites.

q.t: Visually challenged students measure with…
o: Scales with raised markings felt by touch
q.e: Raised markings can be read by touch.

q.t: A pendulum swinging is both oscillatory and…
q.e: It repeats its to-and-fro after fixed intervals.
